Title: Re: New Psyche and Telepathic Tracking

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body:
First of all, Psyche and Telepathic Tracking are played in the same window now, aren't they?

Assuming they are, what happens if the acting minion plays a Psyche, then the reacting plays Telepathic Tracking?

Several possible answers:
-the TT effect kicks in first because the combat does not end. Then is the Psyche remembered until the end of the combat or does it fizzle?
-"Set Next Round" is like Set Range: it cannot be unset once it has been set, so the first card played wins (I like it, it's simple).

The same question might apply to Coordinate attacks too.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> Non-existant user wrote:
> First of all, Psyche and Telepathic Tracking are played in the same window now, aren't they?
>
They will be (as of Jan 01, 2012).*

> Non-existant user wrote:
> Assuming they are, what happens if the acting minion plays a Psyche, then the reacting plays Telepathic Tracking?
>
A new round of combat will happen (TT's "combat does not end"). Psyche!'s "start a new combat after this round" effect is lost (as much as Rotschreck's "send that vampire to torpor after combat has ended" is lost)

> Non-existant user wrote:
> Several possible answers:
> -the TT effect kicks in first because the combat does not end. Then is the Psyche remembered until the end of the combat or does it fizzle?
> -"Set Next Round" is like Set Range: it cannot be unset once it has been set, so the first card played wins (I like it, it's simple).
>
> The same question might apply to Coordinate attacks too.
>
The same replies also apply.

> Lech wrote:
> How they interact with rotshreck now ?
>
No change on that. Rotschreck ends the combat, thus ends the round. You play Psyche! / TT / CA, and a new [round of] combat starts, instead of having your vampire go to torpor.

* EDIT Ankha: For further reference, the window during which Psyche! and Telepathic Tracking are no longer the same. Telepathic Tracking is a replacement effect and is played when the "combat would end" (and it doesn't end anymore). Psyche! is played when "combat is about to end", which only occurs once the replacement effects have been used, and only if the combat is really ending.

Messages.Author: Brum
Messages.Body:
Name: Rötschreck
Cardtype: Master
Master: out-of-turn. Frenzy.
Put this card on a vampire when an opposing minion attempts to inflict aggravated damage on him or her, whether the damage would be successfully inflicted or not. Combat ends. This vampire is tapped and sent to torpor. This vampire does not untap as normal. During this vampire's next untap phase, burn this card.
Artist: Mike Danza

By Rötschreck's text, combat does end, unless players play a Sudden or Wash.
VtES doesn't have a stack of effects or a queue.
Combat ends.
If you rule that Psyche! can only be used inside combat, you can no longer use it here, because combat is not about to end. It ended already.

> I would like to see an explanation that carefully walks us through both Impulse and exact moments of card resolution and effects.

The Impulse isn't relevant. Both players can play an effect in the 'combat is about to end' window, as per the cited ruling on Telepathic Tracking. The impulse only control which goes first when there's a fight.

Telepathic Tracking is playable in this window, per LSJ's cited ruling on the issue, which uses the terminology "Only usable when both combatants are still ready and combat is about to end." Combat is about to end via Rotschreck. Telepathic Tracking is allowed to interrupt it.

A re-written Psyche can use the same wording and work the same way.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
If we were doing it the way you suggest, we would have
- Psyche! can squeeze a combat between the current combat and a combat another Psyche! queued (and you could play any amount of Psyche!'s in the first combat).
- Blissful Agony vs Blissful Agony would be a mess
- IotK vs IotK would be a mess.

The thing about combat is that it isn't an "instantaneous" effect (such as "send to torpor", "tap" or "burn 1 blood").

LSJ tried not to have any stack at all. He managed - through rulings, sometimes - to avoid stacks. If you queue effects that will happen "later", you're creating such a stack. The problem with stacks is that you delay something's resolution.

As would, potentially, "Play when combat is about to end; restart combat" - although that would prevent Obedience. Actually, I think that would open a whole new can of worms.)
